header.userPrompt:
Add an AI document-classification gate at document ingestion, before the expensive models run.
Classify each incoming document from its CHEAP local text using JEV (reuse the existing JevClient
from PR #12 — do NOT add Bedrock or any new dependency), then: (a) reject wrong-type documents with
user feedback before the expensive model, (b) persist + log the classification on every document so a
future parser-routing step can use it, (c) flag likely prompt-injection as an advisory signal. This
was validated by an eval (see ~/jev-metadata-eval): on the app's PDFBox text the type classifier is
correct at ~1.0 confidence on real statements and a real Carrefour ticket; it cleanly separates
ticket vs bank_voucher vs invoice; the injection flag catches overt attacks but is only a signal.

=== 1. DocumentClassifier service (server) ===
New service (e.g. net.wiringbits.services.DocumentClassifier) built on JevClient.choose (single
"choice" question per call; JevChoice has choice + confidence + probabilities). It makes TWO cheap
choose calls on the same text:
  - TYPE: criteria keyed by a new enum DocumentClass -> { bank_statement, purchase_ticket,
    bank_voucher, invoice, other }. Criteria descriptions must match the eval wording:
      bank_statement  = a bank or credit-card ACCOUNT STATEMENT listing many transactions over a period
      purchase_ticket = an itemized store PURCHASE TICKET/RECEIPT: products with prices from a shop
      bank_voucher    = a card-payment voucher/slip: amount, bank, card, authorization/TPV, NO items
      invoice         = a factura/invoice/bill (fiscal/billing details, often says FACTURA)
      other           = none of these / unreadable
  - INJECTION (advisory): criteria { clean, injection_attempt } with the eval's instructions
    (text instructing/overriding the AI, revealing its prompt/secrets, or exfiltrating data).
Return a typed result: DocumentClass + confidence (BigDecimal), plus injectionSuspected: Boolean +
its confidence. DocumentClass is a new enumeratum enum (Uppercase entryNames; fail-loud parse on an
unknown value, like the other enums in the codebase).

FAIL-OPEN is mandatory and intentional (this is NOT a silent default for parsed data — call it out in
a comment): if JevConfig.mode is mock, or JEV errors/429s, or the TYPE confidence is below a
configurable threshold, return an "inconclusive" result that callers treat as "do not block; proceed
to the expensive model". Threshold: add `minConfidence` (default 0.85) to the jev config block in
application.conf with an env override; never log the JEV api key.

LOG every classification with the userId in scope (per the coding-patterns reviewer): the chosen
class + confidence and the injection flag + confidence. If injection is suspected, log a WARNING with
the userId (advisory only — never blocks).

=== 2. Persist the classification (evolution) ===
Add nullable columns to persist the result on BOTH ingestion targets, so it is computed ONCE and is
available later for parser routing / feedback even if not yet consumed:
  - document: ai_classification (text, null), ai_classification_confidence (numeric, null),
    ai_injection_suspected (boolean, null), ai_injection_confidence (numeric, null).
  - bank_statement_draft: the same four columns.
New Play evolution, Ups only, following the repo's evolution conventions (no ';' inside comments,
correct hashing). No CHECK constraints. Update the Anorm DAOs/models/parsers for both tables.

=== 3. Statement path gate — ExtractBankStatementDraftAction ===
In ExtractBankStatementDraftAction.apply, the draft's text is already produced by
`PdfTextExtractor.extract(bytes)` right before the slow/paid `extractionService.extract(...)`. Insert
the classifier between them:
  - Classify `text`; persist the result on the draft (columns above).
  - If the class is confidently NOT bank_statement -> call BankStatementDraftRepository.markFailed(
    draftId, reason, now) with a user-facing reason (e.g. "This looks like a <class>, not a bank
    statement."), and SKIP extractionService.extract. The draft UI already surfaces the `error`.
  - bank_statement / inconclusive -> proceed to extraction exactly as today.
Log with the draft's userId.

=== 4. Ticket path gate — ProcessDocumentAction + ParseReceiptAction ===
PRE-TEXTRACT (ProcessDocumentAction.processReceiptOrInvoice, before textractClient.startExpenseAnalysis):
inject BlobStorage, load the document bytes, run PdfTextExtractor.extract:
  - Right(text) (text-layer PDF, e.g. the Carrefour PDF): classify, persist on the document.
      * Confidently NOT purchase_ticket (i.e. bank_voucher / invoice / bank_statement / other) ->
        documentsRepository.updateStatus(doc.id, DocumentStatus.Unsupported, Some(reason)), send the
        Telegram feedback (below), and SKIP Textract (startExpenseAnalysis is NOT called).
      * purchase_ticket or inconclusive -> proceed to Textract exactly as today.
  - Left (image-only/scan — the common Telegram photo case): proceed to Textract as today (there is no
    cheap text to classify yet). Do NOT persist a classification here.
POST-OCR (ParseReceiptAction, where the Textract AnalyzeExpense output is available): if the document
has NO persisted classification yet (the image branch above), classify on the reconstructed Textract
text and persist it — this is the "classify once if not already classified" step. This is ADVISORY
and FAIL-OPEN: do NOT reject or drop a document that already cost a Textract call; still parse it as
today. If it is confidently NOT a purchase_ticket, send the Telegram feedback so the user learns they
sent a voucher/invoice. (Rationale: the pre-Textract gate only SAVES cost on text-layer PDFs; photos
must be OCR'd regardless, so the post-OCR check is for routing + feedback, not cost.)

=== 5. User feedback on rejects ===
  - Statements: the draft `error` reason (set via markFailed) is already shown in the bank-statements
    draft UI — no new UI needed; just set a clear reason string.
  - Tickets (Telegram): on a reject (pre-Textract) or advisory non-ticket (post-OCR), send a message
    via the existing TelegramApi.sendMessage(chatId, ...) to the originating chat. Recover the chatId
    from the document's Telegram linkage (TelegramReceiptRepository / TelegramRepository, as
    TelegramPhotoAction does). If the document did not originate from Telegram, skip the Telegram step
    (do not fail). Message example: "This looks like a <bank voucher/invoice>, not a purchase ticket —
    please send the itemized ticket."

=== EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE ===
No "contains both ticket + voucher" detection. No custom per-class parsers yet (only persist + log the
class for later). No change to the draft->confirm flow, the AiSuggestions feature, the JEV suggestions
engine, or the statement extraction ladder itself.

=== CONSTRAINTS ===
- Follow docs/guide (antipatterns, backend, data-infra, testing, ci-checklist) and CLAUDE.md.
- Reuse JevClient (#12). NO dependency changes (build.sbt/plugins.sbt/package.json); revert incidental
  yarn.lock churn (dependencies reviewer).
- User-scoped DB access (WHERE user_id = ?) on any new/changed query; stable ORDER BY; no CHECK
  constraints; Chimney for case-class mapping; prefer enums over stringly-typed values; never drop a
  Future; log new user-scoped work with the userId after the user is resolved (coding-patterns reviewer).
- The gate is deliberately FAIL-OPEN; this is the one intentional exception to "fail loud" and must be
  commented as such. Everything else still fails loud.
- Evolutions: Ups-only, follow the repo conventions (evolutions reviewer).
- Attribution: do NOT put any Claude session links (claude.ai/ or Claude-Session) in commits or the PR
  description; `Co-Authored-By: Claude` IS allowed.

=== TESTS ===
- DocumentClassifier: TYPE maps each class to its DocumentClass; injection flag parsed; FAIL-OPEN when
  the JevClient is mock / errors / returns below threshold (use a stub JevClient returning a configured
  choice+confidence — do not hit the network).
- Statement path: a non-statement classification marks the draft failed with a reason and does NOT call
  the extraction service; a bank_statement/inconclusive proceeds; the classification is persisted.
- Ticket path pre-Textract: a text-layer non-ticket sets Unsupported + reason, persists the class, and
  does NOT call startExpenseAnalysis; a ticket/inconclusive proceeds to Textract; image-only proceeds
  to Textract with no classification.
- Ticket path post-OCR: classifies only when not already classified (once-guard), persists, is
  fail-open (never drops the document).
- Evolution applies cleanly.
- Verify per task with targeted `sbt "testOnly *Spec"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`; the final stage
  runs the full suite.

resultJson.description:
Add a cheap, fail-open AI document-classification gate at ingestion. Before the expensive models run (Sonnet/BDA statement extraction for bank-statement drafts, AWS Textract AnalyzeExpense for tickets), each document's cheap local text (PDFBox via `PdfTextExtractor`, or the reconstructed Textract text for image-only tickets) is classified with the existing `JevClient.choose` (from PR #12). There are two choice questions: a TYPE question (bank_statement / purchase_ticket / bank_voucher / invoice / other) and an advisory INJECTION question (clean / injection_attempt). The result is persisted once on `document` or `bank_statement_draft` (4 new nullable columns each) so a later parser-routing step can use it. It is logged with the userId. When the classifier confidently says the document is the wrong type, the document is rejected before the paid call: the draft is marked failed with a user-facing reason, or a text-layer ticket PDF is set to Unsupported, Textract is skipped, and the user gets a Telegram message. Suspected injection is only logged as a WARN, never blocks. No new dependencies and no Bedrock.

The gate is FAIL-OPEN on purpose, and this is the one allowed exception to the repo's "fail loud / no silent defaults" rule. It must be commented as such at the decision point. In any of these cases the caller proceeds exactly as today: JEV in mock mode, a JEV error or 429, either question failing, TYPE confidence below `jev.minConfidence` (default 0.85, env `JEV_MIN_CONFIDENCE`), no cheap text (an image-only PDF or a photo), or the blob missing. The post-OCR classification in ParseReceiptAction is advisory only: it never rejects or drops a document that has already been through Textract. Everything else (DB writes, enum parsing of stored values) still fails loud.

Two choices in this plan differ from the literal wording of the request and are deliberate. Please check them:
(1) `DocumentsRepository.updateStatus(id, status, parserVersion)` takes a parser VERSION as its third argument, and `document` has no error/reason column. So the reject passes `None` there, not the reason. The reason reaches the user via Telegram and the logs, and the persisted ai_classification records why.
(2) The web upload lets users choose kind=`invoice`, and those documents go through the same processReceiptOrInvoice/Textract path today. So the accepted classes depend on the kind: Receipt accepts {PurchaseTicket}, Invoice accepts {PurchaseTicket, Invoice}. Without this, a user's deliberate invoice upload would be rejected, which is a regression.

tasks.description:
Add `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/6.sql`. Start it with `-- !Ups` only, and do not touch 1-5.sql.
- `ALTER TABLE document ADD COLUMN ai_classification TEXT NULL, ADD COLUMN ai_classification_confidence NUMERIC NULL, ADD COLUMN ai_injection_suspected BOOLEAN NULL, ADD COLUMN ai_injection_confidence NUMERIC NULL;`
- The same four columns on `bank_statement_draft`.
- A short comment (no ';' inside comments, UPPER-CASE keywords) saying the value is a DocumentClass entryName such as BANKSTATEMENT/PURCHASETICKET/BANKVOUCHER/INVOICE/OTHER, and that NULL means not classified.
- No DEFAULT and no CHECK.

Models: add flat Option fields `aiClassification: Option[DocumentClass], aiClassificationConfidence: Option[BigDecimal], aiInjectionSuspected: Option[Boolean], aiInjectionConfidence: Option[BigDecimal]` to `repositories/models/Document` and `repositories/models/BankStatementDraft`. You may add a small derived `def classification: Option[DocumentClassification]` if useful.

In daos/package.scala add `implicit val documentClassColumn: Column[DocumentClass] = enumColumn(DocumentClass.withNameInsensitiveOption)`, which fails loud on an unknown value. Add the 4 columns to `documentParser` (Macro.parser column list) and to every SELECT in DocumentDAO (all/find/findById/findBySha256).

In BankStatementDraftDAO add them to the hand-written `parser` and to `selectColumns`.

New user-scoped writes:
- `DocumentDAO.updateClassification(id: UUID, userId: UUID, c: DocumentClassification, updatedAt: Instant)` with `WHERE id = ... AND user_id = ...`, throwing if 0 rows are updated.
- `BankStatementDraftDAO.updateClassification(id, userId, c, updatedAt)`, the same.
- Repository wrappers using `withTransaction`: `DocumentsRepository.updateClassification(id, userId, c)` (clock.instant()) and `BankStatementDraftRepository.updateClassification(id, userId, c, updatedAt)`.
- Write `c.documentClass.entryName`.

Fix any positional `Document(...)` construction in tests (ParseReceiptActionSpec.stubDocument) by adding `None`s.

Test infra: add `bankStatementDrafts: BankStatementDraftRepository` to `core/RepositoryComponents` and RepositorySpec.withRepositories, and add a `createBankStatementDraft(userId, ...)` factory to `utils/RepositoryUtils`. Tests seed data only via RepositoryUtils, not raw SQL.

Tests (Postgres via RepositorySpec):
- DocumentsRepositorySpec: updateClassification round-trips all 4 fields; a new document has them all None; it fails for another user's id.
- New `repositories/BankStatementDraftRepositorySpec`: the same round-trip and user-scoping checks.
- The evolution applies cleanly, which is implied by PostgresSpec applying evolutions.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *DocumentsRepositorySpec *BankStatementDraftRepositorySpec *ParseReceiptActionSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.description:
Inject `documentClassifier: DocumentClassifier` into ExtractBankStatementDraftAction. In `apply`, after `text = PdfTextExtractor.extract(bytes)...` and before `extractionService.extract(...)`:
1. Call `documentClassifier.classify(draft.userId, s"draft $draftId", text)`.
2. If `result.toPersist` is defined, call `bankStatementDraftRepository.updateClassification(draftId, draft.userId, c, clock.instant())`.
3. Branch on `result.rejection(Set(DocumentClass.BankStatement))`:
   - Some(cls): `bankStatementDraftRepository.markFailed(draftId, s"This looks like a ${cls.label}, not a bank statement.", clock.instant())`, with wording adjusted for Other, e.g. "This doesn't look like a bank statement.". Log INFO with `userId=${draft.userId}`, and do NOT call extractionService.
   - None (bank_statement or inconclusive): continue exactly as today.

Keep the existing `recoverWith` (a persistence failure still marks the draft failed, which is fail loud). Prefer a flat for-comprehension, with the branch as a small private method returning Future[Unit]. Never drop a Future. Update the class scaladoc to mention the gate.

Tests in ExtractBankStatementDraftActionSpec: keep the existing toPayload tests and add `apply` tests on RepositorySpec (real Postgres, draft created via RepositoryUtils.createBankStatementDraft) with:
- an in-memory fake BlobStorage holding a text-layer PDF generated in the test with PDFBox (PDDocument + PDPageContentStream + `new PDType1Font(Standard14Fonts.FontName.HELVETICA)`, more than 100 chars of synthetic text, no PII);
- the StubJevClient wrapped in a real DocumentClassifier;
- a StatementExtractionService test double that records calls and returns a canned ExtractionResult. Mockito is acceptable only for this heavy concrete external boundary; otherwise subclass it.

Cases:
- class invoice/purchase_ticket at confidence 1.0: the draft becomes failed with the reason, the classification is persisted, and extraction is NOT called;
- bank_statement: extraction is called, the draft is ready, and the classification is persisted;
- below threshold: extraction is called and the observed classification is persisted;
- JEV failure: extraction is called and nothing is persisted.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *ExtractBankStatementDraftActionSpec"`.

Post-OCR advisory classification in ParseReceiptAction

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- server/ is the Play backend. Flow: controllers → actions (thin orchestration) → repositories (Future + DatabaseExecutionContext) → DAOs (Anorm raw SQL, objects in repositories/daos). Background jobs dispatch to actions by id.
- lib/api/shared/ holds the Tapir endpoints and API models. NOT touched: no API or frontend change. The draft UI already shows draft.error.
- No build.sbt / plugins.sbt / package.json / yarn.lock changes. Revert any incidental yarn.lock churn.

KEY EXISTING CODE
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/JevClient.scala
  - `trait JevClient { def choose(state: String, questionName: String, instructions: String, criteria: Map[String,String]): Future[JevChoice] }`
  - `case class JevChoice(choice: String, confidence: BigDecimal, probabilities: Map[String,BigDecimal])`
  - RealJevClient already validates that the choice is one of the criteria keys, retries 429 twice, and then fails with `JevRateLimitedException`.
  - MockJevClient picks the smallest key with confidence 0; it is bound when jev.mode=mock.
  - Bound in modules/ServicesModule.jevClient. A new @Inject class such as DocumentClassifier needs no module binding.
- config/JevConfig.scala: `case class JevConfig(apiKey: JevApiKey, baseUrl, model, mode: JevConfig.Mode)` with Mode = Mock | Real. `apply(Configuration)` reads it with config.get[...]. Its toString hides apiKey; keep it that way.
  - Positional constructions to update: ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec:25 and RealJevClientSpec:26. Fixture: JevConfigSpec.
  - ConfigModule.jevConfig logs the mode/baseUrl/model.
  - application.conf `jev {}` block at around lines 231-246, using the `key = default` + `key = ${?ENV}` pattern.
- Reference pattern for JEV service + logging style: services/JevStatementSuggestionsService.scala.
- Stub pattern for tests: the `private class StubJevClient ... extends JevClient` in test/.../ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec.scala:28 and JevStatementSuggestionsServiceSpec.scala:26.
- services/PdfTextExtractor.scala: `extract(bytes: Array[Byte]): Either[String,String]`. It returns Left for unreadable or non-PDF bytes (e.g. a JPEG photo) and for text under 100 trimmed chars (scans or blank pages).
- services/BlobStorage.scala: `trait BlobStorage { put; exists; get(storageKey): Future[Option[Array[Byte]]]; delete }`. Prod uses S3BlobStorage, and there is a NoOpBlobStorage. For tests, write a tiny in-memory implementation.
- actions/bankstatements/ExtractBankStatementDraftAction.scala: apply(draftId) runs findById → blobStorage.get → PdfTextExtractor.extract (throws on Left) → `extractionService.extract(label, sha256, storageKey, text)` → markReady. `recoverWith` → markFailed(draftId, msg, now). It skips drafts whose status is not "processing". Draft fields: userId, sha256, storageKey, status (String consts in BankStatementDraft.Status), error.
- services/StatementExtractionService.scala: a concrete class (bedrock/textract/bda clients, ActorSystem). `extract(...)` returns `Future[AiStatementExtractor.ExtractionResult]`. See ExtractBankStatementDraftActionSpec for constructing an ExtractionResult.
- repositories/BankStatementDraftRepository.scala + daos/BankStatementDraftDAO.scala:
  - hand-written RowParser plus a `selectColumns` string (payload::TEXT);
  - markFailed/markReady/findById are internal and unscoped (background job), and stay as they are;
  - user-scoped methods use `WHERE id = ... AND user_id = ...`.
  - There is no BankStatementDraftRepositorySpec yet, and BankStatementDraftRepository is NOT in test RepositoryComponents yet.
- actions/documents/ProcessDocumentAction.scala:
  - apply skips terminal statuses (Parsed / ParseFailed / Unsupported);
  - process() skips BankStatementPdf;
  - processReceiptOrInvoice: updateStatus(Processing) → textractCacheRepository.find(sha256, AnalyzeExpense). A cache hit sets Analyzed + enqueues ParseReceipt; a miss calls `textractClient.startExpenseAnalysis(doc.sha256, doc.storageKey)` + creates a textract_job + enqueues PollReceipt.
  - There is no spec for it yet.
- actions/documents/ParseReceiptAction.scala:
  - `parse(doc)` reads the AnalyzeExpense cache JSON and calls `DocumentParser.parse(cache.response, doc.kind.entryName)`;
  - updates the receipt, merchant and rules, then sets status Parsed;
  - sends a Telegram \"Receipt parsed\" WebApp button via telegramReceiptRepository.findByReceiptId(receipt.id);
  - `notifyTelegramError(documentId, text)` shows the document → receipt → telegram_receipt → sendMessage pattern, with .recover.
  - Its spec (ParseReceiptActionSpec) uses Mockito for the repos and TelegramApi, with a positional `Document(...)` in stubDocument.
- Cached AnalyzeExpense JSON shape (RealTextractClient.serializeExpenseDoc / PollReceiptAction):
  - `{\"ExpenseDocuments\":[{\"SummaryFields\":[{Type{Text,Confidence},LabelDetection{Text},ValueDetection{Text,Confidence}}],\"LineItemGroups\":[{LineItemGroupIndex, LineItems:[{LineItemExpenseFields:[...same field shape...]}]}]}]}`
  - There are NO LINE Blocks. DocumentParser.scala has helpers fieldType/fieldValue/fieldLabel (private).
- repositories/DocumentsRepository.scala: `updateStatus(id, status: DocumentStatus, parserVersion: Option[String])`. The 3rd argument is the PARSER VERSION. The document table has no error/reason column. Also find/findById/findBySha256/all.
- daos/DocumentDAO.scala: 4 SELECTs that list the columns explicitly. `documentParser` in daos/package.scala is Macro.parser[Document] with a column-name list. `enumColumn(f)` in package.scala gives a fail-loud enum column. DocumentStatus uses `enumColumn(DocumentStatus.withNameInsensitiveOption)`.
- models/documents/DocumentStatus.scala is the enum template (enumeratum, `EnumEntry with Uppercase`). Note that Uppercase turns BankStatement into \"BANKSTATEMENT\", so map JEV snake_case keys (bank_statement...) to the enum explicitly.
- DocumentKind: Receipt (\"receipt\"), Invoice (\"invoice\"), BankStatementPdf. Web upload (UploadReceiptAction) allows receipt or invoice. TelegramPhotoAction always creates Receipt.
- Telegram:
  - apis/TelegramApi.scala is a CONCRETE class: `TelegramApi @Inject()(TelegramConfig, ApplicationLifecycle)(implicit ec)` with `sendMessage(chatId: Long, text): Future[Unit]`.
  - TelegramReceiptRepository.findByReceiptId(receiptId): Future[Option[TelegramReceipt(…, receiptId, chatId: Long, …)]].
  - ReceiptRepository.findByDocumentId(documentId).
  - TelegramPhotoAction creates document + receipt + ProcessDocument job first, then the telegram_receipt row. The background job runs on a 1-minute tick, so the link normally exists. If it is missing, skip and log; never fail.
- Evolutions live in server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/. 1-5 exist and are immutable; the next is 6.sql. Template for a column-add evolution: 5.sql (`-- !Ups`, comment, ALTER TABLE). Play computes the hashes; just never edit existing files. Exactly ONE new evolution file for the PR (edit 6.sql if it needs fixing).

CONVENTIONS
- Data rules (docs/guide/data-infra.md):
  - every new or changed query on user-owned tables has `WHERE user_id = ...`;
  - all writes use `database.withTransaction`;
  - timestamps come from the injected `Clock` (clock.instant()), never Instant.now() in main code;
  - no DEFAULT, no CHECK, TEXT not VARCHAR, UPPER-CASE SQL keywords, snake_case;
  - list queries need a stable ORDER BY (…, id).
- Scala patterns (coding-patterns reviewer):
  - never drop a Future: compose everything in the for/flatMap;
  - log with `userId=$userId` once the user is known;
  - prefer enums over strings;
  - use Chimney (`io.scalaland.chimney.dsl.*`) for case-class to case-class mapping when fields line up.
- No silent defaults EXCEPT the classifier's documented fail-open path, which needs an explicit comment saying it is intentional.
- Do not log document text (PII) or the JEV api key.
- Tests:
  - ScalaTest AnyWordSpec + `must` matchers + ScalaFutures `.futureValue`;
  - `\"method\" should { \"behaviour\" in ... }`, never naming the class/spec in descriptions;
  - DB tests extend `net.wiringbits.core.RepositorySpec with utils.RepositoryUtils`, use `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }`, seed via RepositoryUtils (createUser, createDocument(userId, sha256, storageKey, kind, ...), createReceipt(userId) which creates a document + receipt), and pass `(using executionContext, Clock.systemUTC())` to actions;
  - prefer fakes/stubs over Mockito, with Mockito tolerated for heavy concrete external clients (TelegramApi, StatementExtractionService) and in the already-Mockito ParseReceiptActionSpec;
  - no network calls;
  - JSON fixtures must be multi-line and readable;
  - synthetic data only, no PII;
  - there are no PDF fixtures in the repo: build test PDFs in-memory with PDFBox (org.apache.pdfbox.pdmodel.{PDDocument, PDPage, PDPageContentStream}, font `new PDType1Font(Standard14Fonts.FontName.HELVETICA)`), with at least 100 chars for the text branch; a blank page or random bytes give the Left branch.
- Build/verify per task: `sbt \"testOnly *XSpec\"` for the touched specs, or `CI=true sbt Test/compile` (`-Werror`: unused imports and warnings fail). Do NOT run the full `sbt test` during a task. Format with `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`.
- Commits: `Co-Authored-By: Claude` is fine. Never include claude.ai/ or Claude-Session links.

EVAL FACTS (~/jev-metadata-eval/README.md)
- The state was capped at 8000 chars.
- On the app's PDFBox text the TYPE classifier gave 1.0 on real statements and on the Carrefour ticket.
- Textract-text tickets are noisier (hence advisory post-OCR).
- The injection check caught overt attacks but missed a data-exfiltration note, so it is a signal only, never blocking.
